updates.title: OBBBA Makes 100% Bonus Depreciation Permanent for Commercial Real Estate
updates.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act permanently restored 100% bonus depreciation for qualifying commercial real estate components acquired after January 19, 2025. Depreciation recapture applies upon sale under Section 1245.
updates.action: Review component depreciation methods; consider cost segregation studies for properties acquired in 2025-2026

updates.title: Section 179 Expensing Limit Increased to $2.56 Million for 2026
updates.summary: Section 179 deduction limit increased from $1.25M to $2.56M for 2026, with phase-out beginning at $4.09M in total purchases. Pairs with 100% bonus depreciation for full year-one expensing.
updates.action: Maximize equipment purchases in 2026; coordinate with 100% bonus depreciation for maximum tax efficiency

updates.title: QOZ Critical Deadline: December 31, 2026 for Old-Regime Investments
updates.summary: Investors who deferred gains in Opportunity Zones must recognize deferred gain by December 31, 2026, unless rolling into post-2026 investments. New regime begins January 1, 2027 with rolling five-year deferrals and 10% basis step-up.
updates.action: URGENT: Audit all QOZ positions immediately; determine extension vs. new rollover eligibility before year-end deadline

updates.title: Massachusetts Surtax Threshold Increased to $1,107,750 for 2026
updates.summary: The millionaire's surtax threshold rose to $1,107,750 from $1,083,150. The 4% surtax applies to income above this level, creating a combined 9% top rate (5% base + 4% surtax).
updates.action: Review tax planning strategies for owners with income above $1.1M; evaluate income deferral and entity structure optimization

updates.title: Massachusetts Commercial Conversion Tax Credit: $15.3M Awarded for 856 Homes
updates.summary: Governor Healey announced $15.3M in Commercial Conversion Tax Credit awards for the second round of the CCTCI, supporting 856 new homes across Boston, Dedham, Springfield, Westford, and Worcester.
updates.action: Monitor EOHLC for next funding round; evaluate vacant/underutilized commercial properties for conversion eligibility

updates.title: Hard Money Lending: Massachusetts Rates Stable, No 2026 Changes
updates.summary: Massachusetts allows interest rates up to 20% with Attorney General notice; no new usury law changes in 2026. Default legal rate remains 6% unless parties contract higher in writing.
updates.action: Continue existing notification protocols to AG; no operational changes required
